title: Debug on the board from a plain-English request

runs.name: t1_count_write
runs.request: First write 3 to COUNT. Then capture count, win_wr and the shell's ADDR byte when the shell writes the COUNT register (win_wr is 1 and addr is 0x80), 16 cycles before and 32 after. The write that triggers it puts 0x1234 in COUNT. Afterwards read COUNT back.

intent.question: What are count, win_wr, and the shell ADDR byte around the write to COUNT?

runs.plan_text:
Request: First write 3 to COUNT. Then capture count, win_wr and the shell's ADDR byte when the shell writes the COUNT register (win_wr is 1 and addr is 0x80), 16 cycles before and 32 after. The write that triggers it puts 0x1234 in COUNT. Afterwards read COUNT back.
Back end: vendor ILA (one ILA IP, Basic tier), clock domain CLK100MHZ (net CLK100MHZ_IBUF_BUFG, 100 MHz).
Probes:
  win_wr           1 bit   u_shell.u_core.win_wr        <- 'win_wr' (register, trigger) pins u_shell/u_core/win_wr_reg/Q
                 note: the shell writes a design register
  addr             8 bits  u_shell.u_core.frame[1]      <- 'addr' (register, trigger) pins u_shell/u_core/frame_reg[1][*]/Q
                 note: the request's ADDR byte (0x80 + offset for the design's registers)
  count           16 bits  u_dut.count                  <- 'count' (register, data) pins u_dut/count_reg[*]/Q
                 note: the counter itself
Trigger (AND): win_wr == 1 AND addr == 0x80
Window: 1024 samples, 16 before the trigger and 1007 after (the smallest size that holds the 16 before and 32 after you asked for; the answer covers your window).
Ports: probe0 flags 1 bit = win_wr[1]; probe1 data 24 bits = addr[8] + count[16] (2 of the 5 allowed ports; about 1 block RAM tile).
Before arming: write COUNT (0x80) = 0x3
After arming: write COUNT (0x80) = 0x1234
After the capture: read COUNT (0x80)
Can be built (probe set ad3b58a920a1).
runs.answer:
Triggered on win_wr == 1 AND addr == 0x80. Cycle 0 is sample 16 of 1024 at 100 MHz. The capture holds cycles -16 to 1007; this answer covers cycles -16 to 32, as asked.
At cycle 0: win_wr = 1, addr = 0x80, count = 0x0003.
win_wr was 1 at the trigger; high for 1 cycle from cycle 0 (1 of 49 samples high).
addr held 0x80 for the whole window (cycles -16 to 32).
count was 0x0003 from cycle -16 to 0, then 0x1234 from cycle 1 to 32.
Read back over the shell after the capture: COUNT = 0x00001234.
Supply and temperature from the chip's own monitor (XADC) when armed: die 24.7 C, VCCINT 1.006 V, VCCAUX 1.794 V, VCCBRAM 1.006 V; after upload: die 24.9 C, VCCINT 1.006 V, VCCAUX 1.794 V, VCCBRAM 1.006 V; inside the recommended operating conditions (ROC: the data sheet's supply and temperature ranges).

runs.name: t1_pwm_period
runs.request: With COUNT set to 0x8421 and DUTY set to 0x40, record led and phase for one whole PWM period starting when phase wraps to 0: no cycles before the trigger, 1023 after. Then read DUTY and COUNT back.

intent.question: How do led and phase behave over one PWM period after phase wraps to 0 with COUNT set to 0x8421 and DUTY set to 0x40?

runs.plan_text:
Request: With COUNT set to 0x8421 and DUTY set to 0x40, record led and phase for one whole PWM period starting when phase wraps to 0: no cycles before the trigger, 1023 after. Then read DUTY and COUNT back.
Back end: vendor ILA (one ILA IP, Basic tier), clock domain CLK100MHZ (net CLK100MHZ_IBUF_BUFG, 100 MHz).
Probes:
  phase            8 bits  u_dut.phase                  <- 'phase' (register, trigger) pins u_dut/phase_reg[*]/Q
                 note: the PWM phase counter; LED[i] is lit on the clock after phase < duty while count[i] is 1
  led             16 bits  u_dut.led                    <- 'led' (register, data) pins u_dut/led_reg[*]/Q
                 note: the LED outputs (PWM); added in F0B so the ILA can check duty against level
Trigger (AND): phase == 0x00
Window: 1024 samples, 0 before the trigger and 1023 after (the smallest size that holds the 0 before and 1023 after you asked for; the answer covers your window).
Ports: probe0 data 24 bits = phase[8] + led[16] (1 of the 5 allowed ports; about 1 block RAM tile).
Before arming: write COUNT (0x80) = 0x8421; write DUTY (0x81) = 0x40
After the capture: read DUTY (0x81); read COUNT (0x80)
Can be built (probe set a6a9590e41ad).
runs.answer:
Triggered on phase == 0x00. Cycle 0 is sample 0 of 1024 at 100 MHz. The window is cycles 0 to 1023.
At cycle 0: phase = 0x00, led = 0x0000.
phase was 0x00 at the trigger and changed 255 times (256 values, 0x00 to 0xFF); first changes: cycle 4: 0x00 -> 0x01, cycle 8: 0x01 -> 0x02, cycle 12: 0x02 -> 0x03.
led was 0x0000 from cycle 0 to 0, then 0x8421 from cycle 1 to 256, then 0x0000 from cycle 257 to 1023.
Read back over the shell after the capture: DUTY = 0x00000040, COUNT = 0x00008421.
Supply and temperature from the chip's own monitor (XADC) when armed: die 24.9 C, VCCINT 1.006 V, VCCAUX 1.794 V, VCCBRAM 1.006 V; after upload: die 24.7 C, VCCINT 1.006 V, VCCAUX 1.794 V, VCCBRAM 1.006 V; inside the recommended operating conditions (ROC: the data sheet's supply and temperature ranges).

runs.name: t1_sync_byte
runs.request: Trigger on the rising edge of rx_valid when the received byte rx_data is 0xA5, and show rx_data and the raw UART receive line, 900 cycles before and 100 after. Make it happen by reading SCRATCH.

intent.question: What are rx_data and the raw UART receive line around the arrival of byte 0xA5?

runs.plan_text:
Request: Trigger on the rising edge of rx_valid when the received byte rx_data is 0xA5, and show rx_data and the raw UART receive line, 900 cycles before and 100 after. Make it happen by reading SCRATCH.
Back end: vendor ILA (one ILA IP, Basic tier), clock domain CLK100MHZ (net CLK100MHZ_IBUF_BUFG, 100 MHz).
Probes:
  rx_valid         1 bit   u_shell.u_rx.valid           <- 'rx_valid' (register, trigger) pins u_shell/u_rx/valid_reg/Q
                 note: a byte arrived from the host
  rx_data          8 bits  u_shell.u_rx.data            <- 'rx_data' (register, trigger) pins u_shell/u_rx/data_reg[*]/Q
  uart_rx_pin      1 bit   uart_rx_pin                  <- 'uart_rx_pin' (pin, data) pins UART_TXD_IN_IBUF_inst/O
                 note: the raw serial line from the host
Trigger (AND): rx_valid rises AND rx_data == 0xA5
Window: 1024 samples, 900 before the trigger and 123 after (the smallest size that holds the 900 before and 100 after you asked for; the answer covers your window).
Ports: probe0 flags 2 bits = rx_valid[1] + uart_rx_pin[1]; probe1 data 8 bits = rx_data[8] (2 of the 5 allowed ports; about 1 block RAM tile).
After arming: read SCRATCH (0x03)
Can be built (probe set 7b2af61c97ae).
runs.answer:
Triggered on rx_valid rises AND rx_data == 0xA5. Cycle 0 is sample 900 of 1024 at 100 MHz. The capture holds cycles -900 to 123; this answer covers cycles -900 to 100, as asked.
At cycle 0: rx_valid = 1, rx_data = 0xA5, uart_rx_pin = 1.
rx_data was 0x4A from cycle -900 to -869, then 0xA5 from cycle -868 to 100.
rx_valid was 1 at the trigger; high for 1 cycle from cycle 0 (1 of 1001 samples high).
uart_rx_pin held 1 for the whole window (cycles -900 to 100).
Supply and temperature from the chip's own monitor (XADC) when armed: die 25.6 C, VCCINT 1.006 V, VCCAUX 1.794 V, VCCBRAM 1.006 V; after upload: die 25.7 C, VCCINT 1.006 V, VCCAUX 1.794 V, VCCBRAM 1.006 V; inside the recommended operating conditions (ROC: the data sheet's supply and temperature ranges).

runs.name: t1_or_flags
runs.request: Capture count and duty when either win_wr or press_clear goes to 1, 8 cycles before and 64 after. To make it happen, wait 300 ms and then write 0x22 to DUTY.

intent.question: What are count and duty when win_wr or press_clear rises?

runs.plan_text:
Request: Capture count and duty when either win_wr or press_clear goes to 1, 8 cycles before and 64 after. To make it happen, wait 300 ms and then write 0x22 to DUTY.
Back end: vendor ILA (one ILA IP, Basic tier), clock domain CLK100MHZ (net CLK100MHZ_IBUF_BUFG, 100 MHz).
Probes:
  win_wr           1 bit   u_shell.u_core.win_wr        <- 'win_wr' (register, trigger) pins u_shell/u_core/win_wr_reg/Q
                 note: the shell writes a design register
  press_clear      1 bit   u_dut.u_db_clear.press       <- 'press_clear' (register, trigger) pins u_dut/u_db_clear/press_reg/Q
  count           16 bits  u_dut.count                  <- 'count' (register, data) pins u_dut/count_reg[*]/Q
                 note: the counter itself
  duty             8 bits  u_dut.duty                   <- 'duty' (register, data) pins u_dut/duty_reg[*]/Q
Trigger (OR): win_wr rises OR press_clear rises
Window: 1024 samples, 8 before the trigger and 1015 after (the smallest size that holds the 8 before and 64 after you asked for; the answer covers your window).
Ports: probe0 or_win_wr 1 bit = win_wr[1]; probe1 or_press_clear 1 bit = press_clear[1]; probe2 data 24 bits = count[16] + duty[8] (3 of the 5 allowed ports; about 1 block RAM tile).
After arming: wait 300 ms; write DUTY (0x81) = 0x22
Can be built (probe set 5786d4f73d78).
runs.answer:
Triggered on win_wr rises OR press_clear rises. Cycle 0 is sample 8 of 1024 at 100 MHz. The capture holds cycles -8 to 1015; this answer covers cycles -8 to 64, as asked.
At cycle 0: win_wr = 1, press_clear = 0, count = 0x0000, duty = 0x40.
win_wr was 1 at the trigger; high for 1 cycle from cycle 0 (1 of 73 samples high).
press_clear held 0 for the whole window (cycles -8 to 64).
count held 0x0000 for the whole window (cycles -8 to 64).
duty was 0x40 from cycle -8 to 0, then 0x22 from cycle 1 to 64.
Supply and temperature from the chip's own monitor (XADC) when armed: die 26.5 C, VCCINT 1.006 V, VCCAUX 1.794 V, VCCBRAM 1.006 V; after upload: die 26.5 C, VCCINT 1.006 V, VCCAUX 1.794 V, VCCBRAM 1.006 V; inside the recommended operating conditions (ROC: the data sheet's supply and temperature ranges).

runs.name: t1_reuse_rise
runs.request: After arming, write 0x0042 to COUNT. Capture count on the rising edge of win_wr, 4 cycles before and 8 after, then read COUNT back.

intent.question: What count value is captured around the rising edge of win_wr, and what is the COUNT register value after capture?

runs.plan_text:
Request: After arming, write 0x0042 to COUNT. Capture count on the rising edge of win_wr, 4 cycles before and 8 after, then read COUNT back.
Back end: vendor ILA (one ILA IP, Basic tier), clock domain CLK100MHZ (net CLK100MHZ_IBUF_BUFG, 100 MHz).
Probes:
  win_wr           1 bit   u_shell.u_core.win_wr        <- 'win_wr' (register, trigger) pins u_shell/u_core/win_wr_reg/Q
                 note: the shell writes a design register
  count           16 bits  u_dut.count                  <- 'count' (register, data) pins u_dut/count_reg[*]/Q
                 note: the counter itself
Trigger (AND): win_wr rises
Window: 1024 samples, 4 before the trigger and 1019 after (the smallest size that holds the 4 before and 8 after you asked for; the answer covers your window).
Ports: probe0 flags 1 bit = win_wr[1]; probe1 data 16 bits = count[16] (2 of the 5 allowed ports; about 1 block RAM tile).
After arming: write COUNT (0x80) = 0x42
After the capture: read COUNT (0x80)
Can be built (probe set 597f16f6d572).
runs.answer:
Triggered on win_wr rises. Cycle 0 is sample 4 of 1024 at 100 MHz. The capture holds cycles -4 to 1019; this answer covers cycles -4 to 8, as asked.
At cycle 0: win_wr = 1, count = 0x0000.
win_wr was 1 at the trigger; high for 1 cycle from cycle 0 (1 of 13 samples high).
count was 0x0000 from cycle -4 to 0, then 0x0042 from cycle 1 to 8.
Read back over the shell after the capture: COUNT = 0x00000042.

limits: Vivado 2026.1 Basic licence tier: one ILA instance per design, so one clock domain per build, and at most 5 probe ports, and each port has one comparator (measured).
Trigger compares are per bit (0, 1, X and rising/falling/either edge); != and magnitude compares on buses are refused unless they reduce to a per-bit pattern; OR only across 1-bit terms.
A new probe set is a new build (418.1 to 531.8 s for these 5 T1 builds, one each); trigger, window and stimulus are run-time settings.
One design (T1) and five requests; the parser was not measured on a held-out set of requests.
Clocks made inside the design (MMCM outputs) and signals inside generate blocks are not resolved yet.
XADC samples are read through JTAG at arm and after upload, not on the capture timeline.
No agent role is offered the debug tools yet: offering them needs its own pre-registered evaluation first.

agent_vs_owner.owner: asked for the capability, the order (front end first) and the safety rules (SRAM only, power and temperature limits, DRCs never skipped)
agent_vs_owner.agent: wrote the front end, the tests and the docs, ran the builds and board runs; a language model (the project's cheap default) only turned each request into the intent JSON
